name: browser
title: Browser
description: Pages in tabs, as a browser has, e.g. for the panel beside a conversation (its bar in barContainer where given: an AgentApp titlebar's row over the panel, each pane's bar over its pane; its first tab and its toolbar on one start line, its last button and the toolbar's on one end line, 12px in; there its tabs as a desktop browser's on the frame: the one shown a solid piece 32px high of the panel's colour (a step lighter in dark), the others bare with a thin line between two, a piece of their own under the pointer, each with its close; as wide as 15rem, narrower as more open); its toolbar of islands, back, forward and a web page's reload one, the page's tools another, its address a pill ringed thinly only where the keyboard brought the focus (not a click, nor a new tab's focus as it opens): web pages in a frame (its sandbox the app's) or the app's own; code (a CodeViewer), diffs, images, video, audio, PDFs, tables (a CSV), terminals and folders in their viewers. Each tab goes back and forward through what was opened in it, or is one of the app's fixed areas (pinned: no close button); a diff of more than one file lists them over the one picked, with the app's actions (Discard, Commit) in a bar at its foot; on coarse pointers the diff shows its file icon, name and translatable Unified label even with the file list, with signs alone and no numbers or hunk headers; touch tabs have equal segments, across the bar on phones and content-wide from 640px; its toolbar (or its viewer's) says where the page is, and a web page's address can be changed: every address, typed or a recent one, goes through resolveAddress (by default resolveWebAddress, http for a local host and its port, https for the rest), and the empty bar says what it takes. A web page (a frame, the app's screenshot of it, or a remote browser's live page: its frames pictures drawn once decoded, a canvas the app draws into or a video it plays, the reader's pointer, wheel, keys, an input method's composition and paste sent back in the page's CSS pixels, its cursor, and its select popups and script dialogs drawn by agentui; by touch, the screen's keyboard only while the page has a caret) shows in the panel's size or a device's, with whether its server runs (or a page saying nothing does, or that it did not load, with Retry), the agent at work in it (what it does, its pointer, the reader taking over), the reader pointing at an element of it for the chat, a dark color scheme kept by tab, and its console and requests in a fixed 250px drawer with an always-visible tool (disabled without data): agentui draws the chrome, the app gives the states. The app opens pages (a new tab, or in the tab shown) and changes them as they load or grow; the state is the browser's own or the app's. A page in a viewer is named by its tab, not again in the viewer's toolbar (back and forward alone at its start; a folder keeps its path, the way up), where it is on the tab's hover.
